# Overall Goal

Explore the bank marketing data in a static way before building the Shiny app.
The data comes from a Portuguese bank where each row is one client and `y` corresponds to whether the client subscribed to a term deposit.
I want to explore which client traits (such as age, job, and education) and campaign details (such as call duration and number of times contacted) are associated with in a client subscribing.
I will use contingency tables, numerical summaries, and plots to explore the data. The idea is to find patterns in this exercise before building them into the interactive app

## Setup

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)

```

## Read the data

```{r}
train <- read_delim("data/train.csv", delim = ";")
test <- read_delim("data/test.csv", delim = ";")
nrow(train)
nrow(test)
```

Per project instructions combine the training and testing rows.

```{r}
bank_all <- bind_rows(train, test)
nrow(bank_all)

```

Because we are combining the data, it is a good idea to check if there are any duplicates. Also Kaggle specifically mentions this 
"test.csv: 4521 rows and 18 columns with 10% of the examples (4521), randomly selected from train.csv"

Let's remove the duplicates 
```{r}
bank_all <- distinct(bank_all)
nrow(bank_all)
```

Now we are back to 45211 rows so the stacking training and test was never needed, also we confirmed above from Kaggle.
